Your observatory

A quality change applies when you next reload. Scientific pixels are unchanged.

Sound always starts muted and requires your click. These are original synthesized interface effects, not sounds recorded in space. Scientific inspection is silent. Reduced-motion preferences disable camera travel animation.

Follow your curiosity.

Start with SPHEREx. Other observatories are an optional collection. Select a telescope and follow Light → Instrument → Universe. Published images are sourced examples; SPHEREx also connects to the installed real observations through the same scientific instrument. Drag to orbit, scroll or pinch to zoom. Arrow keys rotate; + / − zoom; Home resets; Escape returns from a focused workspace.

Three distinct environments: Solar-system positions, orbital circles and object sizes are schematic, without live ephemerides. Infrared-sky markers use actual ICRS directions on a sphere, with no measured 3D distances. Decorative stars are not a catalogue or survey coverage.

Entering an observation: the scene recedes and a native observation instrument appears. Immersive and Classic View share exactly the same investigation. Its real dates, wavelengths, conservative quality masks, source hashes, questions and evidence exports remain available. Return to the sky and resume without losing questions or the viewport.

Only the restricted M101 area currently offers a two-date review comparison. Qualified scientific approval remains PENDING. A visual difference is not a discovery.

Models with a source.

Reusable NASA models and textures are educational context. They do not supply SPHEREx science pixels. Models may be simplified historical visualizations. No NASA Eyes application assets were extracted.

Three.js r180: MIT · Draco: Apache-2.0 · Manrope, Source Sans 3 and retained Outfit: SIL Open Font License. All runtime assets and licenses are stored locally.
